narrative_obligations.detail: Selin must acknowledge Bora's help through action, not instant intimacy.
The same notebook must return to Selin by the end.

artifact.prose:
Selin crossed the school courtyard with her field notebook pressed between both hands. The wind tugged at her jacket and sent the first cold drops of rain against her face, but the greenhouse was only a short distance away.

A sudden gust struck harder. The notebook flipped out of her grip before she could close her fingers. It skimmed across the courtyard, pages fluttering wildly, then sailed through the open greenhouse door.

“No!” Selin ran after it.

Through the doorway, she saw the same notebook lying open on the greenhouse floor. Rain began tapping faster around her.

“The side path is quicker,” Bora called, catching up. He pointed toward the clear path running beside the greenhouse.

“I can get there myself,” Selin said. She started toward the front, but another gust made her brace her feet. The longer way now seemed especially long.

Bora was already heading along the side path. “This way.”

Selin looked from him to her notebook inside the greenhouse. She did not like needing help, especially from a classmate she hardly trusted. Still, he knew where he was going.

“All right,” she said reluctantly. “The side path.”

She followed Bora along it, matching his quick pace as the rain thickened. Together they reached the greenhouse entry and stopped at the open door.

Selin could still see her notebook on the floor inside, its paper pages shifting in the draft. She glanced at Bora.

“Your route helped,” she admitted.

He gave a small nod. They stood at the entry, ready to go after the notebook.
